title: Daily Market Digest
subtitle: Review of Friday, August 28, 2026 Trading Session

sections.title: Market Pulse: Fed Inflation Concerns Weigh on Stocks

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Dip on Friday as Fed Chair Signals Potential Rate Hikes
items.summary: U.S. equities closed lower on Friday, August 28, 2026, as investors processed hawkish remarks from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh regarding persistent inflation. Major indices saw modest declines, with the Nasdaq Composite experiencing the largest percentage drop among the three primary benchmarks. Market sentiment was largely influenced by the anticipation of potential interest rate hikes as the Fed prioritizes bringing inflation under control. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Elastic Surges on Strong Earnings
items.summary: Elastic ($ESTC) shares soared 24.3% following a report of better-than-expected fiscal Q1 earnings and an upbeat full-year guidance.

items.headline: Gap Jumps on Raised Guidance
items.summary: Gap ($GAP) shares climbed 14.3% after the apparel retailer surpassed second-quarter profit expectations and increased its full-year earnings guidance.

items.headline: Affirm Rallies on Earnings Beat
items.summary: Affirm Holdings ($AFRM) jumped 10.2% after the fintech company reported a strong beat on fiscal fourth-quarter earnings and provided an optimistic forward guidance.

items.headline: PayPal Drops as Takeover Bid Abandoned
items.summary: PayPal ($PYPL) shares fell 13% following reports that Advent and Stripe had abandoned their $50 billion takeover bid for the company.

items.headline: Broadcom Plummets Amid Tech Retreat
items.summary: Broadcom shares plummeted over 11% as major technology stocks broadly retreated on Friday.

items.headline: Nvidia Slides on Profit Taking
items.summary: Nvidia ($NVDA) shares slid over 3% amid profit taking and a general downturn in major technology stocks.

items.headline: Fed Chair Warsh Delivers Hawkish Tone at Jackson Hole
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh, in his debut Jackson Hole speech, emphasized the central bank's commitment to tackling inflation. He noted that while the economy 'appears to have strengthened,' inflation remains 'hot' and above the 2% target, hinting at possible interest rate hikes in the upcoming September meeting to bring prices under control.

items.headline: Consumer Sentiment Declines, Inflation Remains a Concern
items.summary: U.S. consumer sentiment dropped in August, falling 6.3% to 51.7 from July, driven by persistent concerns that high inflation will continue. This data point reinforces the challenges facing the Federal Reserve in achieving its price stability mandate.

items.headline: Consumer Discretionary Leads, Tech Lags Amid Broad Sector Shifts
items.summary: On Friday, the consumer discretionary sector emerged as the top performer, gaining 1.69%, with strong showings from companies like Domino's Pizza and Amazon. Conversely, information technology was the worst-performing sector, declining 1.29%, contributing to the broader market's negative close. Financial stocks saw modest gains of 0.4%, while real estate lagged, falling 0.5%.

items.headline: Crude Oil Prices Rise on Supply Considerations
items.summary: Brent crude oil December futures increased by 1% to $92.38 per barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) November futures rose by 1.2% to $89.37 per barrel. Geopolitical factors, specifically ongoing Iran-Oman talks over the Strait of Hormuz, continue to introduce potential supply considerations.
